overview: Two-arm parallel randomised trial of the perioperative glucose protocol against usual care in adults with insulin-treated diabetes having elective surgery at one teaching hospital.
population: Adults with insulin-treated diabetes listed for elective general, orthopaedic or urological surgery with an expected stay of at least one night.
exposure: Protocol arm: dose-adjustment table at pre-assessment, nurse call two days before surgery, first-on-the-list scheduling where the specialty allows, subcutaneous correction scale for operations under three hours. Usual care arm: current variable practice.
procedures: Randomisation 1:1 at pre-assessment by a central web system, stratified by specialty. Capillary glucose recorded at admission, before induction, in recovery and four-hourly for 24 hours, with laboratory confirmation of values below 4 mmol/L.

outcomes.name: Glucose out of range on the day of surgery
outcomes.measure: Any capillary value above 12 or below 4 mmol/L from admission to midnight
outcomes.why: Captures both dangers the protocol targets.

outcomes.name: Theatre list disruption
outcomes.measure: Operations moved or cancelled because of scheduling changes
outcomes.why: Scheduling must not disrupt other patients.

feasibility: At about 150 eligible patients a year and 48 percent recruitment, about 72 patients a year would be randomised.

biasFlags.label: Contamination between arms
biasFlags.note: The same staff care for both arms.

biasFlags.label: Incomplete ward glucose documentation
biasFlags.note: Failed in a comparable pilot trial.

summary: Two-arm trial protocol with one primary outcome.
